reviewed.text: White throws near the bar, plays a checker, and picks up before the cube discussion. The pale dice overlap the point and rail in the footage.
One pale die has a single central pip. White moves the checker from 9 to 2, requiring 6–1.
Black’s dice stay in the same locations through the detection gap at 3:42. Keep the later face reading on the original roll.
Black moves 9/3 and 6/1. The two verified positions require 6–5. One die was misread as four by the detector.
Black rolls after White picks up, then moves checkers. The die near the bar reads 1; the other face is blurred.
One dark die shows one. Black’s verified transfer from 9 to 3 requires 5–1.
The two dark dice show three and one in repeated original-camera crops. Black hits the blot on the way to the one-point.
White rolls from the bar and picks up without entering. One die reads 6.
Black bears two off from the 3- and 1-points. White remains on the bar.
White shakes out two dice and picks both up without entering. Both faces are blurred.
Black clears the 6-point by bearing off once and moving the second checker to the 3-point.
White rolls from the bar and picks up without entering. One die reads 1.
Two stationary dark dice show 3 and 1 in consecutive original-camera views.
With the starting and resulting boards visible, Black bears one off from point 22 and shifts another from 23 to 24 in fixed numbering. White remains on the bar.
White stays on the bar and the board is unchanged through pickup. One face is five. Carry the verified checker counts from Black’s bear-off.
The same verified board from White’s fan supplies Black’s starting position for this throw. The played move remains unconfirmed.
Black rolls and plays between White’s two throws. The two faces cannot be confirmed by sight.
Black’s short 2–1 on the right leaves the checker on the bar.
Black rolls 6–1, handles the checkers on the far edge, and picks up before White rolls.
Black rolls and moves checkers between two White turns. One die is readable as 4.
Two stationary dark dice show 4 and 3 in consecutive original-camera views.
